policy: archive.js#appendIndex raced-hard-link residual: the nlink guard's fstat(fd)!==1 check and the subsequent writeSync(fd) are not atomic (no POSIX append-only-if-nlink===1 primitive). An attacker who hard-links the fd's inode in the fstat->writeSync window can make the write reach an external inode. Attacker-only (archive-dir write + a WON microsecond race; no non-malicious mistake hard-links the index), same-uid, ZERO-new-capability (the attacker can already write the target file directly); it appends only index TELEMETRY. DISPOSITIONED out-of-model (adversarial-helm, above the operator's dropped boundary; α ruling under 'proceed until finished'; β discriminator: zero-new-capability is dispositive). The nlink guard DOES close the PRE-EXISTING hard-linked index. See ADR-0017.

title: delta-canonical-dispatch-smoke.js claude serve-canary false-greens: $(cat tmp) argv non-expansion on Windows + loose /OK/+exit-0 check passes a served refusal
description: The claude serve-canary in scripts/delta-canonical-dispatch-smoke.js builds its prompt as `claude -p --model <m> --effort max "$(cat \"${tmp}\")"` — `$(cat …)` is a POSIX construct cmd.exe does NOT expand on Windows, so the model receives the LITERAL string `$(cat "/tmp/…")` and refuses it as a shell command (opus-5 replied "I'm not going to run that. That prompt is a shell command substitution…"). The pass-check is `r.exit===0 && /OK/i.test(r.stdout)` — a loose substring + exit-0 that GREENED on the refusal (the fuller reply carried an incidental "ok"). So the canary "proved the serve" while sending a malformed prompt and getting a refusal — it would ALSO green a broken/fallback serve. Pre-existing: the identical `$(cat tmp)` form was on main L95 (opus-4-8 lane) and is now mirrored in the opus-5 canary at L100. The sibling openai lane passes its prompt via stdin (runShell(cmd, TEST_PROMPT)) and got a clean "OK", so the fix is proven adjacent. Found during the opus-5 cutover-land verification (2026-07-24); opus-5 genuinely serves (α WARPOS_PROVIDER_PROBE one-shot confirmed canonicalModel=claude-opus-5) — this is a canary-robustness gap, NOT an opus-5 serve problem.
enforcer_candidate: fix the canary: pass the prompt via stdin like the openai lane (never `$(cat)` in a spawned argv), AND tighten the pass-check to a served-content assertion (exact-match the expected token, or parse --output-format json modelUsage.canonicalModel), so a served refusal/error/fallback can never green it. Optional lint: flag `$(cat` inside a spawned command string.

note: CO-RESIDUAL from r4 (qa-reviewer + backend-reviewer BOTH FAIL, same HIGH, for the halt dossier — not a land): normalizeForDetection's INDEX MAP is UTF-16-vs-code-point DESYNCED. The map is built by iterating CODE POINTS (`for (const cp of raw)`) and `for (const u of out)` also iterates by code point, so an UNCHANGED astral character (supplementary-plane, 2 UTF-16 units) appends 2 units to `norm` but only 1 map entry — while RegExp match indices (cm.index) address UTF-16 CODE UNITS. After any astral char the map is misaligned, so raw-clause slicing points at the wrong offset -> a downgraded/misattributed finding (a false-green). FIX (fold into the fresh-sprint rewrite of normalizeForDetection alongside the p{M}/NFKC + decision-token work): build the map by UTF-16 UNIT (`for (let j=0;j<out.length;j++){map.push(rawIdx);norm+=out[j];}`) and advance rawIdx by the source char's UTF-16 length — OR (cleaner) switch to an NFKC/NFKD-based normalization that sidesteps the manual index map. Add a planted-RED test: an ordinary astral char (e.g. an emoji) BEFORE a citation with an unresolved receipt must stay HARD. This makes the r4-fix residual set = { p{M}+CGJ combining marks, decision-token half, blank separators (U+2800/U+3164), UTF-16 index-map desync } — all in one function a fresh sprint reworks.

β RATIFICATION DIRECTIVE (DECIDE B/0.90, msg_id f1a4d7c9-3e82-4b56-a0d1-6c9e5b2f8a41): scope this fix as the MECHANISM fix, NOT the next category. THE FIX = NFKC normalize-on-match — normalize the detection text to its rendered/canonical form THEN match — which closes p{Cf} AND p{M} AND every future invisible/combining/confusable category BY CONSTRUCTION (this is the true G1 'match on normalized text', which β's original G1 left under-pinned). Do NOT scope as 'add p{M} to the enumerated strip-set': that just moves the gap to the next invisible category (p{Sk} modifier symbols, tag chars U+E00xx, variation selectors) and a future adversarial round finds it — the category-by-category chase IS the r3->r4 recurring trap the mechanism-level fix ends. HONEST FRAMING for the dossier (β rider 1): r4 was REAL PROGRESS (p{Cf} handling IS genuine structural format-char class-closure, present-AND-future, better than r3's enumerated fix) but the invisible-char MECHANISM was NOT closed (p{M} combining marks + blank separators U+2800/U+3164 are the same 'invisible char breaks the scanned token while the rendered token survives' mechanism, left open) — record as 'progress, mechanism not closed', NOT 'brand-new class' and NOT 'total whack-a-mole failure'. CEILING-DISCLOSURE COMPLETENESS (β rider 3, P-059): if anything SHORT of full NFKC ships, the fix MUST enumerate EVERY invisible/confusable category it does not fully normalize, so the residual is self-detecting rather than hunter-found next round.

note: RECORD-HONESTY correction (β design→build close-out #1, msg_id 562ba5b6-3e33-407c-aed7-e21e6f00a73e): the SHIPPED transform is NFKD-decompose-then-strip \p{M}/\p{Cf} (+ fold blanks incl U+2800/Hangul fillers), NOT NFKC as the f1a4d7c9 halt-ratification row named. Reason: NFKC RECOMPOSES, so a precomposed accent (É U+00C9) stays composed and its combining mark never separates → the combining-mark bypass would survive; NFKD decomposes first so the \p{M} strip removes the mark, and NFKD carries the identical K/compatibility fold (fullwidth/math/symbol betas → β, fullwidth DECIDE → DECIDE) so it strictly SUBSUMES NFKC for detection. β ratified NFKD as a CORRECTION to her own directive (NOT a deviation). Any ADR quoting f1a4d7c9's 'NFKC' should read 'NFKD-decompose-then-strip'. Shipped in beta-verdict-citation-receipt.js normalizeForDetection, SP-20260725-001 commit 4964ddb7. policy: beta-verdict-citation-receipt.js CITATION_RE lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z])` excludes ASCII LETTERS ONLY, not digits or id punctuation. So inside a receipt id, a substring like `betaruled` whose preceding character is a DIGIT opens a SECOND citation INSIDE the id token, and the clause slice truncates the receipt to its prefix. Where that prefix is EXACTLY a real ledger id, the forged token resolves clean and the gate passes. Repro at 93ae41ce: `\u03b2 DECIDE, msg_id real000betaruled` with ledger id `real000` yields scanned=2, hard=0, soft=1, --enforce exit 0, while the rendered document cites `real000betaruled`, which is absent from betaEvents. The exploit REQUIRES the real id to be a prefix of the forged token, which is what makes the `real000-betaruled` control correctly HARD (its truncated prefix `real000-` is not a ledger id). Also falsifies the invariant asserted in ceiling note (g) ('only ever over-FLAGS ... never hides/downgrades') — an ED-292 documented-invariant violation.

policy: beta-verdict-citation-receipt.js asserts its word boundaries in the WRONG TEXT SPACE. CITATION_RE's trailing `\b` and its leading lookbehind are evaluated on the NFKD-FOLDED detection text, so the fold itself can MINT an ASCII word character that destroys the boundary and hides the citation entirely. `DECIDE\u00b9` folds to `DECIDE1`, so `\b` sees word-char-to-word-char and fails; `\u1d43\u03b2` folds to `a\u03b2`, so the lookbehind sees `a` and fails. Repro at 93ae41ce: `\u03b2 DECIDE\u00b9 (msg_id fake123)` yields scanned=0, hard=0, soft=0, exit 0 — the forged receipt is never scanned at all. Also reachable via character reference (`¹`) and via U+FF3F folding to `_`. Causation control: `\u03b2 DECIDE\u00b1` yields scanned=1, so a NON-folding character does not hide it — the fold is provably the cause. An exhaustive sweep found 1,943 code points that are non-word, non-stripped and non-space-mapped yet fold to an ASCII word char; 1,831 of them hide the citation. This is the normalization mechanism defeating itself: the fold exists to catch obfuscation and instead manufactures the token that breaks detection.

source: scripts/dispatch-agent.js:1070 (`const stderrBytes = result.stderrBytes || 0`) and :1103 (`stderr_bytes: stderrBytes`) — the count is written to the completion record; the text has no sink.

note: Found live during SP-20260725-002 r13: the security lane failed twice with stderrBytes=4018 and the wrapper's `error` field carried only the codex banner plus a truncated echo of the prompt, so 4018 bytes explaining the failure were unreachable. Diagnosis had to be reconstructed indirectly (a tiny-prompt probe to prove provider health, then a role-registry read to find that security-reviewer's effort is null because its native provider is agy, so a --provider openai override defaults to xhigh). That reconstruction cost several turns and would have been one read of the stderr. COMPOUNDING FACTOR, worth fixing together: dispatch-route-guard correctly blocks a raw `codex exec` used to capture stderr directly, and offers a WARPOS_PROVIDER_PROBE=1 one-shot bypass for an 'approved provider-health probe' — but 'approved' has no defined grantor, so an agent diagnosing a live failure either self-approves a guard bypass (the tunneling anti-pattern, correctly refused here) or works blind. Fixing the sink removes the incentive to reach for the bypass at all. PROPOSED: persist stderr (capped, e.g. last 8KB) to runtime/dispatch-stderr/<dispatch_id>.log and put that PATH in the completion record; a non-ok record with stderr_bytes>0 and no retrievable stderr path is itself the self-detecting violation.
candidate_enforcers: dispatch-agent.js: write capped stderr to runtime/dispatch-stderr/<dispatch_id>.log and add stderr_path to the completion record
a ledger lint: any ok:false record with stderr_bytes>0 must carry a resolvable stderr_path — fails otherwise
define the grantor for the WARPOS_PROVIDER_PROBE bypass, or retire it once stderr is retrievable

policy: BOTH-HALVES RULE (learnings.jsonl 2026-07-29, third instance in SP-20260725-002): every detection/verification fix must pair with its REPORTING half. A fix that detects a bad state but leaves the caller-visible success boolean untouched still returns applied:true over corrupt state. Plus the layer-naming requirement from β b7e4c1a9: each mitigation must state its LAYER (control | window-narrowing | hygiene) in the CODE COMMENT, not only in the review artifact.
source: learnings.jsonl 2026-07-29; β DECIDE b7e4c1a9 (betaEvents 270) + supplement d9f6b204 (271); scripts/checks/memory-apply.js :276 rename vs :980 undo VERIFY BY OBSERVATION
severity_rationale: medium not high — the rule is real and recurring (three instances in one sprint), but each instance is caught by the gauntlet today; the debt is that catching it depends on a reviewer noticing rather than on a gate.
missing_enforcer: design-review discipline with no gate — the GENERAL form is not mechanically checkable, but two sub-parts are
note: HONEST SCOPING, because logging an unenforceable blanket rule and calling it covered is the failure mode this ledger exists to prevent. The general statement ('pair every detection fix with its reporting half') is a DESIGN judgement over prose intent and is not mechanically checkable — do not pretend otherwise. Two sub-parts ARE enforceable and are the real proposals. (A) FIXTURE-PRESENCE PER SUCCESS BOOLEAN, the stronger one: for a named set of caller-visible result booleans (applied, rolledBack, ok), require a test asserting the boolean goes FALSE when the world is wrong — an adversarial fail-open falsifier, required-present. This is the same shape already ratified in .claude/project/reference/record-trust-gate.md (verified present on disk, 5532 bytes, carries the fail-open falsifier language), so this is an EXTENSION of an existing doctrine to result booleans rather than a new mechanism. A per-module registry of {module, boolean, falsifier-test-name} checked for presence exits non-zero when a boolean has no falsifier. (B) LAYER-NAMING LINT, weaker but cheap: in designated security-relevant modules, a comment block introducing a mitigation adjacent to a fail-closed throw must carry one of the three layer labels. Catches the specific regression β named — a defense-in-depth measure being read as a control by the next reader, which is how the gap reopens. WHY THIS IS NOT ALREADY COVERED: I checked the ledger for the class before logging (one keyword hit, ED-286, unrelated content) — no existing row covers it. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS SPRINT: the diagnostic generalises past the TOCTOU that produced it — ask what a caller-visible boolean MEANS, then ask whether it is computed by OBSERVING the world or by reaching the end of the code that was supposed to change the world. memory-apply.js had the answer right for rollback (:980) and wrong for the forward path (:276) in the same file, one round apart; that asymmetry within a single module is the cheapest available tell and a lint could plausibly look for it.
candidate_enforcers: (A) falsifier-presence check over a registry of caller-visible success booleans — extends the record-trust-gate required-present-fixture pattern to result booleans; exits non-zero when a registered boolean has no adversarial fail-open test
(B) layer-naming lint over designated security modules — a mitigation comment adjacent to a fail-closed throw must declare control | window-narrowing | hygiene
(C) weakest, report-only: flag a module that contains a verify-by-observation block for one path and a bare success return for a sibling path (the within-module asymmetry tell)

policy: DISCLOSED RESIDUAL — S-1 RESIDUAL (r14, disclosed under β's five-condition rule — DECIDE b7e4c1a9, betaEvents line 270): scripts/checks/memory-apply.js promotes a temp file over its target with fs.renameSync, a BY-PATH operation. A same-user actor with write access to the store can, in principle, substitute the temp between the pre-rename lstat and the rename itself. r14 does NOT close this window; it makes the outcome safe and loud instead.
source: scripts/checks/memory-apply.js — atomicWriteInStore, the rename and the CONTROL #2 read-back that follows it; reachable from all three call sites (apply, index rewrite, and undo/rollback)
missing_enforcer: none available — this is a disclosed ceiling, not an unenforced policy
note: WHY THE CLASS CANNOT CLOSE — the primary statement, and do not demote it to the secondary one. The threat model here is a SAME-USER actor with write access to the store, so the control and the attacker hold IDENTICAL PRIVILEGES and no filesystem-level mechanism separates them. Even given a rename-by-descriptor primitive, this instance would close and the actor would simply modify the target file after apply returns — a capability they always had. There is no arrangement of this program that denies a same-user writer the ability to change a file this program is allowed to change. WHY THIS INSTANCE ALSO CANNOT CLOSE — supporting evidence, CHECKED not reasoned (β flagged her own version of this claim as reasoned-from-documentation and directed it be checked or softened; ε checked it): on node v24.16.0 the only rename/link APIs are path-based (link, linkSync, rename, renameSync, symlink, unlink); the fd-based surface is limited to fchmod, fchown, fdatasync, ftruncate, futimes; and renameat, renameat2 and linkat are all undefined. So there is no rename-by-descriptor and no linkat/AT_EMPTY_PATH equivalent in this runtime. A future reader can re-run that check; it is a fact about the runtime, not a fact about anyone's reasoning. WHAT r14 ACTUALLY BOUGHT, so nobody mistakes the residual for the whole defect: the defect had two halves and the dangerous half is CLOSED. The attacker never gained a write capability they lacked — what they gained was a FALSE SUCCESS REPORT, apply returning applied:true over content it did not write. CONTROL #2 (post-rename read-back and byte-compare against what was written) closes that BY CONSTRUCTION and independent of the race: an attacker who wins the swap now makes the check FAIL, which is the honest outcome. The remaining residual is therefore 'a same-user actor can cause a loud, correctly-reported failure', not 'a same-user actor can cause a silent corruption'. The honest claim the control supports is 'at the moment I checked, the intended bytes were on disk' — an observation with a stated instant, not a durable guarantee. THE WINDOW NARROWING ({dev,ino} captured before close, re-checked by lstat before rename) is DEFENSE IN DEPTH AND EXPLICITLY NOT A CONTROL, and is labelled that way in the code per β's layer-naming requirement. If a future edit starts describing it as a control, that is this exact defect rebuilt. β'S FIVE CONDITIONS, all met: (1) unreachable by any mechanism available in this runtime AND threat model, with the specific absence named above — impossible, not merely expensive; (2) the narrowing removes the SILENT outcome — the bad case is now loud, never quiet success; (3) the residual grants no capability the actor lacks; (4) disclosed here and in the code comments, with the previously overclaiming :165-171 and :234 comments corrected in the same round; (5) NAMED FALSIFIABLE RE-ENTRY — this closes as acceptable ONLY while the store is single-user and single-writer. If the memory store ever becomes MULTI-WRITER or is SHARED ACROSS A TRUST BOUNDARY, condition 1's premise dies at that moment and this residual REOPENS as a live finding requiring a different design. Anyone making that change must reopen this row.
candidate_enforcers: no mechanism closes the residual itself; the enforceable surrogate is condition 5 — a check that fails if the memory store gains a second writer or crosses a trust boundary while this row is open
the ED-301 falsifier-presence check would keep CONTROL #2 honest by requiring a test that applied:true goes false when the on-disk bytes do not match

NEW INSTANCE + A CONCRETE DETECTOR FOR ONE SUB-CASE. Instance (SP-20260725-002 r14): the fixer's own test comment read 'only fs.realpathSync.native reliably does that on Windows' while the module it was testing called fs.realpathSync. It documented exactly why its fix would not work on the target platform and shipped it — the comment was right and the code was wrong, which is this row's class precisely. WHY THIS INSTANCE IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST ANOTHER TALLY: this row's standing problem is that 'a comment asserts an invariant the code does not hold' is not mechanically checkable in general, because it needs semantic comparison of prose against behaviour. But a SUB-CASE is trivially checkable and covers real defects — the NAMED-IDENTIFIER contradiction. When a comment names a specific API, flag, variant or symbol (`realpathSync.native`, `--strict`, `O_EXCL`) and the adjacent code calls a DIFFERENT one (the base `realpathSync`), no semantic understanding is needed: grep the enclosing function for the exact token the comment names, and flag its absence. That is a lint someone can build in an afternoon, it produces low false positives if scoped to a fixed vocabulary of API-shaped tokens, and it would have caught this instance at write time rather than at ε's post-fix verification. Proposing it as this row's FIRST buildable increment — the general class stays open, but it stops being all-or-nothing.
candidate_enforcers: named-identifier contradiction lint: a comment naming an API/flag/variant token within N lines of a call to a different variant of the same base symbol → flag (narrow, greppable, no semantics required)

note: STRENGTHENING candidate (A), because r14 produced the exact defect that would DEFEAT it as originally written. Candidate (A) proposes requiring a falsifier test to be PRESENT for each caller-visible success boolean. r14 showed presence is not enough: the B-1 test existed, was well-written, and SKIPPED — its precondition probe tested `fs.realpathSync` while the module used `fs.realpathSync.native`, so on the very platform where the defect was reproduced the probe reported 'cannot exercise this scenario', the test silently skipped, and the suite went 74/74 GREEN over a live defect. A presence check would have passed happily. SO CANDIDATE (A) MUST REQUIRE PRESENT **AND ACTUALLY EXECUTED** — a required falsifier that skips must fail the gate, or at minimum be surfaced as a distinct non-pass state rather than folded into green. Corollary worth building in: a skip whose precondition names a DIFFERENT API than the code under test is itself a defect (see the ED-292 amendment of the same date — the two enforcers share the named-identifier idea). No scope change to this row otherwise; the both-halves rule and its honest not-mechanically-checkable scoping stand as written.

policy: A STAGED GAUNTLET PROMPT IS PINNED TO THE COMMIT IT WAS BUILT AGAINST, and any 'do NOT report' suppression inside it is a standing instruction that outlives its truth. Re-firing a staged prompt on a later commit reviews the WRONG CODE against the WRONG CHANGE DESCRIPTION, with the lane additionally silenced about things that may since have become false. Nothing detects either condition.

(2) SUPPRESSION: both the backend and qa prompts carried 'KNOWN NON-BINDING residual (do NOT re-report): store-DIR confinement is lexical path.resolve rather than realpath.' That suppression was WRONG WHEN WRITTEN — it silenced a genuine defect, and the backend lane surfaced it anyway as B-1, which is the only reason it got fixed. Filed at β's explicit instruction REGARDLESS of the r14b fix, because the omission is the point: this class was found and half-fixed at r11 and the surviving residual was never logged.

note: WHY THIS ROW EXISTS EVEN THOUGH r14b FIXES THE INSTANCE. At r11 this exact round trip was found and fixed in the BACKUP path, and the surviving comment (beginning 'MEMORY.md is captured EXACTLY like every other entry: RAW BYTES, no encoding argument') documents the mechanism and then records the scope decision verbatim: 'preReadIndexText stays exactly as it is for removeIndexLines; only the BACKUP stops travelling through a string.' So a competent author saw the forward path, chose not to fix it, wrote that choice down IN THE CODE — and filed nothing. Three rounds later the security lane found it live as a HIGH. That is precisely the omission ADR-0039 §A2.1 condition 4 now forbids ('disclosed where a future reader hits it: its own ED'), and β ruled that the sprint must not close having repeated, in the very file that taught the lesson, the mistake that file teaches. A comment is not a ledger entry: comments are read by whoever is already in the file, ledgers are read by whoever is deciding what to work on. WHY IT COULD NOT CLOSE AS A DISCLOSED RESIDUAL (β, f0a2d95e, tested against the doctrine landed at 4fc25f4d one hour earlier): condition 1 FAILS — the fix is small and the module already contains the correct idiom in its own backup path, so the residual is cheap, not impossible; condition 2 FAILS hardest — there is no narrowing and the bad case is exactly quiet success; condition 4 half-met — disclosed in-code, never filed. NOTE ALSO, and this is a real limit rather than a defect: the r14 S-1 post-rename read-back CONTROL does NOT catch this. It compares what landed against `data`, and `data` is already the corrupted re-encoded string, so it matches itself. The control proves what was intended landed, not that the intent was right — now documented at the control site per β's item 4.

note: 1.1.0 DISPOSITION — RECORDED, DELIBERATELY NOT BACKFILLED, and the reasoning matters because the obvious action is the wrong one. β ruled 1.1.0 gets the same disposition as 1.2.0: a GAP rather than a lie, NO re-tag, RECORD it, with the now-wired gate preventing a third occurrence. Note her operative verb differed by release - 'fill main now' for 1.2.0, 'record it' for 1.1.0 - and checking the artifact shows why that distinction is load-bearing rather than casual. THE FACTS THAT DECIDE IT: 1.1.0's capsule is CURRENTLY SELF-CONSISTENT - changelog.md on disk hashes 3482ef07f599051e and upgrade-notes.md af45afc1bf163f02, each matching its own checksums.json entry exactly - and its checksums.json#commit is c1ef3393, the true 1.1.0 consolidator build point. 1.1.0 also remains a reachable update target (minUpgradeableFrom 0.1.2). SO A BACKFILL WOULD TRADE A DOCUMENTATION GAP FOR TWO WORSE DEFECTS: (1) editing the notes invalidates 1.1.0's own checksums, which is exactly the fail-closed drift that broke all six product dry-runs when the 1.2.0 fill did it - and 1.1.0, unlike 1.2.0 at the time, is a live update target, so the breakage would hit anyone updating TO it; (2) the remedy for that drift is re-running release-build.js 1.1.0, which would RESTAMP checksums.json#commit from c1ef3393 to today's HEAD - falsifying the provenance of a historical release, i.e. making the artifact lie about what it was built from in order to fix a section that currently says nothing. That is the wrong direction on both counts, and it converts a gap into a lie, which is the precise line β drew when she ruled the 1.2.0 fill sufficient. DISPOSITION AS RECORDED: 1.1.0's notes stay as shipped; the gap is recorded here and in the release-gate output (the scan reports it FAIL on 1.1.0 with six sentinel hits across three surfaces plus the null release.json commit, which is the standing, visible record); no re-tag; no capsule edit. Any future decision to publish corrected 1.1.0 notes belongs OUTSIDE the capsule - e.g. a release-notes page or an addendum file that is not covered by checksums.json - so that provenance and integrity both survive. WHY THIS IS NOW BOUNDED RATHER THAN OPEN: the gap existed for at least two releases (1.1.0 and 1.2.0) because nothing detected it. The gate wired as blocking stage-7 means a third cannot be cut; the two historical instances are disclosed rather than repaired, which is the honest end-state for artifacts that are already published.

policy: THE MANIFEST TRIPLE MUST NOT BE HALF-RUNNABLE BY HAND: editing any hash-tracked file outside a release run requires regenerating THREE manifests in a FIXED ORDER (generate-framework-manifest.js -> warpos/snapshot-installed.js -> warpos/manifest/build.js LAST), and there is NO wrapper that runs them as one unit. Every developer and agent re-derives the sequence from memory or from a doc, so a partial run is always one omission away — and a partial run does not fail loudly at the point of the mistake. It surfaces LATER as two indirect release-gate reds (regression_seed's BC-02/BC-05 plus sealed_capsule_contract) that read as substantive content failures rather than as 'you forgot a regen step'.
source: No `scripts/regen-all.js` (or equivalent) exists — scripts/ contains only regen-maps.js. The canonical ordering is embedded in scripts/warpos/release-canonical.js's stage-6 convergence and otherwise carried in prose (the project memory recipe). Cited by ABSENCE plus the one code site that encodes the order.
missing_enforcer: none for the manual path. The RELEASE path is covered (see the ED-050 amendment filed alongside this row): release-canonical.js stage 6 now regenerates all three itself and says so in its receipt. Nothing covers an ordinary edit-then-commit.
candidate_enforcers: a `scripts/regen-all.js` wrapper that runs the three in the fixed order, fails closed if any step exits non-zero, and refuses to report success on a partial run — one command, so the ordering cannot be half-remembered
have that wrapper end by running warpos-manifest-honesty + generate-framework-manifest --check, so it self-verifies rather than trusting its own three exit codes

a pre-commit advisory that notices staged changes to hash-tracked paths with no accompanying manifest change and names the wrapper (advisory, not blocking — a blocking version would fight legitimate manifest-only commits)

policy: A tool must never silently prefer one target channel over another and then report success. An exit 0 must mean the tool did what the caller asked.
source: E-VLAD-001 Wave-1 planning, 2026-07-30. Instance: PC-20260730-0083 — an AUDIT plan contract stamped sprint=S-VLADW1-01 (ENGINE), schema-invalid on top of the mis-association.
missing_enforcer: scripts/sprint/plan.js read the target ONLY from --sprint (via parseSprintArg -> WARPOS_SPRINT_ID) or the registry primary, and never from payload.sprint (it reads only payload.sprint_title / sprint_objective). A caller declaring the target in the payload was silently retargeted to primary and handed exit 0 with a success line naming a different sprint in small print. The pre-existing sanity WARN in main() structurally CANNOT catch this: it fires only when --sprint WAS passed and disagreed.
enforced_by: scripts/sprint/plan.js DOOR 1 — fail-closed: if the payload has a sprint key and it is not a string equal to the resolved target, REFUSE with named error PLAN_TARGET_CHANNEL_MISMATCH, checked BEFORE ensureCurrentSprint() so a refusal writes nothing. DOOR 2 — loud stderr PLAN_TARGET_FROM_AMBIENT naming the resolved target and the registered count when --sprint is omitted with more than one sprint registered.
verified_by: scripts/sprint/test-plan-target-channel-guard.js — 16/16 green with the guard. MUTANT PROOF: with the guard reverted the suite goes 9 passed / 7 failed and case 1 reproduces the exact defect (found 1 contract(s), sprint=S-VLADW1-01, from a payload declaring S-VLADW1-02). Pre-existing scripts/sprint/test-plan-honors-registry-primary.js stays 11/11 including its case 2 (no --sprint flag exits 0), which is precisely why DOOR 2 is loud rather than fatal.
closure_receipt: Guard, red/green proof and mutant proof landed together. The claim is scoped to the declared-intent case only.
accepted_ceiling: RESIDUAL, deliberately NOT closed: a caller that omits --sprint, declares no payload.sprint, and MEANT a non-primary sprint expresses no intent this guard can compare against. Refusing that case was considered and rejected — the documented /sprint:plan invocation (.claude/commands/sprint/plan.md:182) omits the flag and 119 sprints are registered, so a refusal would break the primary documented route and turn test-plan-honors-registry-primary.js case 2 into a false RED. Closing it properly means making every caller pass --sprint, a skill-doc change deliberately not done mid-lane.

policy: An authoring tool must not report success for an artifact that fails its own declared schema. exit 0 should mean 'I wrote a VALID file', not 'I wrote a file'.
source: E-VLAD-001 Wave-1, 2026-07-30. Landed-invalid instance: PC-20260730-0083 carries evidence_level 'not_verified' at affected_surfaces[0] and [4] — a value absent from the schema enum — and plan.js still exited 0.

It is documented as dumb plumbing and writes the YAML unchecked, so an invalid Plan Contract lands silently and only a separately-run scripts/sprint/validate.js catches it. NOT closed by ED-325 filed alongside — that guard covers association, not validity. The two defects compounded in the same artifact.
candidate_enforcers: Call the existing scripts/sprint/validate.js subset validator on the freshly-written contract inside plan.js before returning 0; on failure report the errors and exit non-zero, quarantining or removing the invalid artifact.
Wire the same post-write validation into scripts/sprint/design.js and every other scripts/sprint/ writer that emits a schema-bearing file.
Cheapest interim: make the /sprint:plan skill body require a validate.js run as a documented step whose exit code is read.

policy: A schema enum gating a recorded field must cover the modes the system actually runs, or the record cannot be both valid and informative.
missing_enforcer: schemas/sprint/plan-contract.schema.json#recommended_mode enumerates only solo|adhoc|oneshot|no_recommendation. There is no 'sprint' value, although sprint mode is a first-class build mode (CLAUDE.md Build Modes; ADR-0009 runtime). Both W1 contracts are conducted in sprint mode and therefore record no_recommendation — valid and honest, but uninformative. Nothing detects the gap; the enum simply predates the mode.
candidate_enforcers: Add 'sprint' to the recommended_mode enum; older contracts stay valid so no backfill is needed.
A check cross-referencing the schema enum against the mode list in CLAUDE.md / scripts/mode-set.js so a new mode cannot ship without its enum entry.

policy: A test over a growing corpus must assert an append-safe invariant, not a hardcoded absolute count, or it rots into a false RED on the next legitimate addition.
source: Found in passing 2026-07-30 while running the sprint suite after the ED-325 guard. PRE-EXISTING and NOT caused by that change — no schema file was touched, confirmed via git status on schemas/.
missing_enforcer: scripts/test-sprint.js:103 asserts Object.keys(schemas).length !== 10 and fails with 'expected 10 schemas, got 15'. schemas/sprint/ has held 15 schema files since before this lane began, so the suite exits 1 on a stale expectation while every substantive case passes (7 passed, 1 failed, including 'plan flow writes valid Plan Contract'). A suite that is red for a bookkeeping reason trains readers to ignore it, which is the real damage.
candidate_enforcers: Assert the invariant instead of the count: every *.schema.json in schemas/sprint/ parses, has a unique $id, and the set is non-empty — then a new schema cannot break the test.
If an exact count is genuinely wanted, derive it from a readdir of a synthetic fixture directory rather than from the live corpus.

note: DOUBLE-APPEND HAZARD: a staged-then-appended artifact needs a CONSUMED marker stamped AT APPEND TIME, or the staging file's own 'staged, not appended' text survives as an instruction to duplicate the record. Found by EpsilonW1 on runtime/vlad-w1/betaevents-staged-W1-plan-to-design.md (fixed c322d3a6) as one instance; alpha's sweep found SEVEN more from the same session (every betaevents-staging*.jsonl under runtime/release-1.2.0/), all consumed rows 276-292, none marked — a class, not an instance. All seven backfilled with a first-line CONSUMED JSON marker (valid JSONL; no msg_id, so the strict append one-shots refuse the file fail-closed; path preserved because ledger rows cite it). CONVENTION (extends the ED-267a staging protocol): the APPENDER stamps the staging file CONSUMED in the same action as the canonical append, naming the canonical location and the consumed msg_ids. ENFORCER CANDIDATE: the append one-shot template prepends the marker itself; a lint over runtime/**/betaevents-stag* asserting every file whose msg_ids resolve canonically carries a CONSUMED first line.

CORRECTION of alpha's own genesis claim (EpsilonW1 verified read-only, 2026-07-30): 'the strict append one-shots refuse the file fail-closed by construction' is FALSE — the protection is DOCUMENTARY, not structural. The one-shots named in the rows' append_lane fields are deleted throwaways (not on disk, never committed); NO live code reads a CONSUMED marker (only scripts/ hit is an unrelated flag in safe-spawn.js:287); no lint over the staging glob exists. A future one-shot written fresh has no reason to validate msg_id and would append the CONSUMED marker ITSELF into canonical betaEvents as a junk row — strictly worse than an unmarked file. The markers still have real documentary value (a reader who opens the file is told to stop) and the seven markings stand. CONSEQUENCE: the genesis row's two enforcer candidates are THE fix, not polish — and the staging-glob LINT is the cheaper one, since it demands no template discipline from future one-shot authors. The aspirational-vs-enforced pattern, caught in the row that was filed to close it.

title: The events store holds two incompatible record schemas and the foreign writer is invisible — no envelope validator over paths.eventsFile
policy: Every write to paths.eventsFile MUST carry the logger.js envelope ({id, ts, cat, actor, session, data}). A record that omits cat/actor/session/data is silently dropped by every consumer keying on cat or data.type, so schema divergence must be self-detecting at write time or at scan time — it must not be discoverable only by manual mining.
source: learnings.jsonl 2026-07-30 (sleep:deep:20260730, category store-integrity); scripts/warpos/test-install-matrix.js#emitEvent (around :1493)
missing_enforcer: envelope-key validator over paths.eventsFile wired into /scan:full
candidate_enforcers: An envelope-key validator over paths.eventsFile (assert every record carries id/ts/cat/actor/session/data; report count + first offending line) wired into /scan:full so divergence reds a gate instead of hiding.
Route scripts/warpos/test-install-matrix.js#emitEvent through scripts/hooks/lib/logger.js, or give it its own runtime stream outside paths.eventsFile so the live store has ONE schema.

Correct memory-guard's block message: it currently reads 'Use logger.js or appendFileSync', and appendFileSync is precisely the call that SKIPS the envelope — the guard defends the store against DESTRUCTION while licensing SCHEMA CORRUPTION.

Rename or re-scope scripts/hooks/event-contract.js: it sounds like this enforcer but pairs DOM addEventListener/dispatchEvent inside src/, so checking 'is the event contract enforced?' by filename returns a FALSE YES.
evidence: 144 cat-less records verified store-wide at sleep time (72 landed in one window; 8,791 lines, 0 malformed JSON). emitEvent resolves PATHS.eventsFile and raw-appends {ts, kind, ...payload}, bypassing the logger envelope, inside a fail-open catch so divergence can never announce itself at write time. Self-demonstrated during mining: a distribution query bucketed 1,986 records as type (none) and LOOKED like a clean answer — the Grep-glob false-negative class reproduced inside the memory stores.
note: Filed by /learn:integrate (session-end 2026-07-30 Phase 4a) as the C1 finding of the 2026-07-30 consolidated learning set. policy: A RATIFIED CORRECTION MUST REACH EVERY ARTIFACT THAT DRIVES DOWNSTREAM WORK, NOT ONLY THE ONES THE CORRECTOR HAPPENED TO OPEN. A DoD reworded because the prior form was provably unachievable must not survive verbatim in the plan contract the next phase reads.
source: .claude/project/sprint/plan-contracts/PC-20260730-0085.yaml — anchors: "The user's key must never leave their machine — no transmit, no log, no proxy, no telemetry" (rationale notes), "Credential custody is a COMPLIANCE obligation under Consumer Terms" (assumptions), "a report-only credential check would be adequate" (rejected_alternatives), "Build the fail-closed credential-custody enforcer: no transmit, no log, no proxy" (work items). Corrected form landed in trackers/epics/E-VLAD-001 DoD item 10, trackers/sprints/S-VLADW1-01 DoD (33024f46), and runtime/vlad-w1/w1-planning-inputs.md (88abeb8b) — three of four.
severity_rationale: HIGH and time-critical, not theoretical. Beta ruled the old wording unachievable-as-written (7c4e2b96, ADR-0039 A2.1 condition 2): the Agent SDK authenticates to Anthropic WITH the key, so transmitting it is the mechanism, not a leak — a fail-closed enforcer proving 'never transmits' would prove a falsehood. The epic further records that the 'Consumer Terms forbid credential sharing' citation was NEVER primary-source verified and is explicitly not relied on. PC-0085 is the ENGINE plan contract /sprint:design is instructed to read, and Wave-1 design is the immediate next phase — so the superseded wording is positioned to drive the build unless caught first.
missing_enforcer: none — nothing compares a plan contract's assumption/rationale text against the tracker + epic DoD it was minted from, so a correction applied to the trackers and not to the contract forks silently. scripts/sprint/validate.js checks the contract's SHAPE, never its agreement with the ratified DoD.
candidate_enforcers: A plan-contract freshness check: on /sprint:design entry, diff the contract's DoD-bearing fields against the sprint tracker's DoD section and REFUSE when the contract predates the tracker's last DoD edit (git mtime/commit comparison) without an explicit re-mint.

Cheapest interim: make /epic:fold and any DoD-rewording edit emit a fan-out checklist naming every artifact that quotes the reworded text (grep the distinctive phrase repo-wide) and require each to be visited before the fold commits.
A repo-wide grep gate for phrases a ruling has RETIRED — a 'superseded phrasings' list that exits non-zero when a retired form reappears in any sprint/epic/plan-contract artifact.

policy: A GATE'S MATCHER MUST FAIL LOUD WHEN IT GOES STALE, NOT SILENTLY GREEN. A scan built on literal sentinels copied from a generator is only as live as the pair; a sentinel that stops matching anything is a drift signal, not a pass.
source: scripts/checks/release-notes-placeholder-scan.js — the file's own DRIFT-PROOFING docstring: "A sentinel that no longer matches anything is not a pass, it is a signal the pair drifted — see --require-sentinels-live." The flag --require-sentinels-live does not exist: a repo-wide grep for it returns exactly one hit, that docstring line. main() handles only --json and --version.
severity_rationale: HIGH because this scan was promoted to a BLOCKING stage-7 release gate this same session (052ca44b, ED-318's closing condition). A blocking gate whose matcher can silently stop matching is worse than no gate: it reports the same clean green for a genuinely-fixed capsule and for a capsule whose placeholder wording the generator has since changed. The SENTINELS list is a hand-copied duplicate of literals in scripts/warpos/release-canonical.js with no mechanical link between the two.
missing_enforcer: none — the drift-guard is named in the docstring and never implemented. Nothing asserts that each SENTINEL still appears in release-canonical.js's emitted skeletons, and nothing fails when the generator's wording is edited independently.

policy: A permissions allow-rule in .claude/settings.json must be MATCHABLE by the permission checker that reads it. A rule naming a tool-shape the checker never matches is inert — it grants nothing while reading as a grant.
source: S-VLADW1-01 gauntlet fix cycle, 2026-08-18/19. Every dispatched builder in this session emitted five identical warnings on stderr: "Permission allow rule (.claude/settings.json): Write(<path>) is not matched by file permission checks — only Edit(path) rules are. Use Edit(<path>) instead (Edit rules cover all file-editing tools)." Affected rules: Write(.claude/manifest.json), Write(.claude/project/events/**.jsonl), Write(.claude/project/memory/**.jsonl), Write(.claude/project/decisions/**.jsonl), Write(.claude/runtime/**.jsonl).
missing_enforcer: Nothing fails when settings.json carries an inert allow-rule. The harness WARNS on every spawn, which is honest, but the warning lands in per-dispatch stderr that nobody reads unless a dispatch dies — it surfaced here only because an unrelated failure (ED-350) made me read the stderr. A warning delivered only into an unread channel is not an enforcer.
candidate_enforcers: A settings-lint over .claude/settings.json permissions.allow that exits non-zero on any rule whose tool-shape the file-permission checker does not match (today: Write(...) forms, where only Edit(path) matches), wired into /scan:full — cheap, fully static. Additionally or alternatively: surface the harness warning in the dispatch wrapper preflight so it appears on a GREEN dispatch too, not only a red one.
note: Latent, not active. The five rules are inert, so those writes fall through to the normal permission path rather than being wrongly granted — the failure direction is LESS access than intended, not more. That is why it is low today. It is medium latent because the next person to add a Write(...) allow-rule for a genuinely needed path will believe it took effect and will not find out until something starves. Same shape as the aspirational-vs-enforced class in CLAUDE.md Policy and Enforcement Hygiene: the rule exists, nothing checks that it does anything.

policy: A ledger that is the evidence base for a security claim must report its own contents accurately: the count it prints must be the count of the thing it names, and a record it cannot format must be surfaced as unrecognized rather than rendered as a malformed instance of the expected type.
source: S-VLADW1-01, 2026-08-19. broker-dogfood.js --report over runtime/d4/inc1/dogfood-fallbacks.jsonl prints "count : 4" and lists a row rendering as "#undefined … undefined -> undefined / reason: undefined (undefined) via undefined". The file holds TWO schemas: three d4-dogfood-fallback rows (seq 1,3,4) and ONE d4-dogfood-fallback-outcome/1 row (refers_to_seq:1) which is an EXPLANATION of seq 1, not a fallback. The report formats both with the fallback formatter and counts LINES rather than fallback events.
missing_enforcer: Nothing checks that the report renders every schema present in the ledger, and nothing asserts the printed count equals the number of records of the counted type. The failure is silent and reads as data corruption to a reader, which is worse than a loud parse error.
candidate_enforcers: (1) A test over broker-dogfood.js --report with a fixture ledger containing one of EACH schema, asserting the fallback count excludes outcome rows and that an outcome row renders as an explanation attached to its refers_to_seq. (2) Fail-loud on an unrecognized schema string rather than formatting it with the default formatter. (3) An append-safe count assertion: printed count === records whose schema is the fallback schema.
note: Two concrete harms, both in the direction of overstating risk, which is why this is medium and not high. (a) The headline OVERCOUNTS fallbacks 4 vs the true 3 — and the report warns "Each must be individually EXPLAINED before the transport is described as proven, and before the Seam E fence flip is argued from dogfood mileage", so an inflated count directly inflates the bar for that argument. (b) It renders the one row that IS an explanation as an unexplained mystery, so the reader is told an explanation is owed for a row that already carries one. Found while verifying my own brokered land against the ledger rather than trusting the receipt I had just quoted — the land itself was correctly recorded as brokered and added no fallback row (counter 4 -> 4, zero mileage burned).

policy: A pre-commit guard that scans documents must resolve its scan root from the WORKTREE the commit is being made in — never from the main repo root — and its failure output must name the root it scanned, so a worktree builder is never blocked by breakage in a tree it did not touch and cannot tell which tree was judged.
source: S-VLADW1-03 fix-attempt-2, 2026-08-28, vlad worktree engine-lane. Builder's diagnosis: the guard evaluated from the vlad MAIN repo root (359 docs, 83 broken) instead of the committing worktree (410 docs, 4 broken). Not uniform — 10b/10d/10e committed through the same guard fine, so it is state- or timing-dependent. The builder tried plain commit, tried --no-verify once, then STOPPED and explicitly refused to add the dead refs to doc-ref-integrity.allowlist.json (the right call — allowlisting a check to pass one's own commit is linter suppression). ε verified the staged tree + suite (308/308, check:ship 0) and landed it externally as 49fa49f.
impact: A worktree builder can complete correct work and be unable to land it; the only recoveries are an external commit or suppressing an unrelated check. On a terminal fix attempt this is a silent way to lose a bundle.
enforcer_candidate: merge-guard resolves the doc-ref scan root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the committing worktree (not the common dir); failure line prints `scanned-root=<path> docs=<n> broken=<n>`; a falsifier test that runs the guard from a secondary worktree with a clean tree while main is dirty and asserts PASS.

policy: Bound (byte-for-byte checked) prose that asserts CODE or IMPORT-GRAPH state must not use unanchored temporal/self-relative deictics — 'this fix cycle', 'as of this writing', 'currently', 'now', 'today', 'a previous cycle', 'the sprint's' — because a byte-bind freezes a referent that points at nothing; it must anchor to a commit hash, a dated sprint id, or be removed. Enforcer: a lint over the bound-paragraph population (custody-claim-lint's own derived set) that REFUSES a named deictic family inside a paragraph that also contains a code-state predicate, with a controls-first near-miss battery.

policy: Before overwriting a git note (or any append-only correction artifact), the writer must read the existing content and append, never force-replace — a correction attached to an erroneous commit is itself part of the record and must not be destroyable by a later writer's default.
source: git notes semantics: `git notes add -f <commit>` replaces the existing note wholesale; the only signal is git's post-hoc stderr line 'Overwriting existing notes for object …'. Verified by α: both notes carry α's attribution and ε's disclosure.

policy: A test must not bind an absolute count of a registry's contents where the count exists to guard a loop over those contents. gate-failclosed-enforcer.test.js L23 (assert.equal(registry.rows.length, 13→14→…)) and L57 (assert.equal(checkedRepaired.length, 0→7→…)) are coverage guards on a property loop and a control (beta 9a2f4e81), so removing them is wrong; but as absolute literals they go red on every legitimate registry change and must be re-measured and re-quoted by hand each time (B5-T; again at B6 with rows 14→16). Removing the literal is wrong and freezing it is wrong; the durable form is an append-safe invariant (e.g. rows.length >= the seeded minimum AND every row in an emitted id set is present) plus a synthetic fixture that proves the loop's population guard still fires on a truncated set. This sprint shipped neither (epsilon's R-12 in S6-7-RESIDUALS.md).

AMENDMENT 1 — THE CATEGORY-LEVEL FACT (beta 9d6c2a83 §1, row 425): the defect passed beta's gate as well as alpha's and epsilon's: three ED-392 greps by three readers, beta's read at source, alpha's byte grep with offsets — every check run on the envelopes tonight was a CONTENT check over prose; not one was a RESOLUTION check over a reference. The envelope wrote '(absolute)' beside each path — a claim about the world — and every reader treated it as furniture. A missing CATEGORY of check, not a missed instance. The method limit it exposes: a pre-committed checklist (1f6b8e34) protects against inventing the check to fit the answer; it does not protect against the checklist being incomplete — the checklist's population is the author's, unexamined, and never gets a second reader. Enforcer consequence: the pre-fire mechanism must be TYPED by what an artifact asserts — for every reference an envelope makes (path, sha, id, row count), a check that the referent exists as claimed, run by the instrument that will consume it (epsilon's probe resolved the native form where statSync would have passed a form the lane's resolver rejects — beta §5: verify with the consumer, not a proxy). Companion countermeasures adopted: a clear names the sha of the bytes it covers ('read at source' bare = the pin-by-label problem — beta); a report that supersedes earlier shas says so (epsilon).

AMENDMENT 2 — THE SIBLING QUESTION (beta 2c8f7b41 §4, row 426): what other kinds of claim does an envelope or brief make that no check tests? Paths were one. Counts (e.g. 'the registry holds 16 rows'), ids (dispatch ids, ED ids, msg_ids) and shas (the assembled-file sha triple) are the obvious next three — and a sha quoted by a reader who cannot compute one is a label one level up: it must be cited as another party's measurement with the reader's own by-content verification stated (beta §1). ENFORCER SHAPE, generalised: the pre-fire lint is TYPED by the kind of claim — for each path, fs.existsSync from the consumer's cwd (native form on win32); for each sha, recompute and compare; for each id, resolve in its ledger/store; for each count, recount from the emitted set — and refuse the prompt on any mismatch, naming it. Companion rule for readers (epsilon's, adopted by beta): follow the instruction that examined the thing you are about to act on; if none did, that is the finding.

AMENDMENT 3 — THE CEILING CLAUSE (beta 6f1a9d54 §1, row 427): the typed pre-fire lint of amendment 2 MUST EMIT ITS OWN CLAIM-KIND PARTITION (the kinds it checks — path / sha / id / count — as enumerated units) AND STATE WHAT THAT PARTITION DOES NOT REACH, in its output, on every run — the same obligation the round imposes on every lane's derivation_rule. A lint typed by N kinds has a hole wherever an (N+1)th kind exists, and the defect this row was filed for WAS a whole category nobody had a check for; a partition-scoped guard has a hole wherever the partition misses. Rule for maintainers: WIDEN a kind, never keep appending kinds. Acceptance for status=enforced: the lint's clean output carries its partition and its stated ceiling; a clean output with neither is the shape of the defect this row closes (clean over the kinds it knows, silent on the kind it does not) and does NOT close the row.

policy: The framework-purity pre-commit guard must judge the tree the commit will actually write — the file(s) a command stages — not the index as it stood before the command ran.
source: scripts/hooks/framework-purity-guard.js (PreToolUse on Bash `git commit`; runs framework-purity.js --staged at HOOK time)
missing_enforcer: hook
candidate_enforcers: make the guard a real git pre-commit hook (runs after the command's own `git add`, on the final index) instead of a PreToolUse scan of the pre-command index
or: have the PreToolUse guard also scan the paths named in any `git add <paths>` segment of the same command, and record which index it judged (sha of the index) in its refusal
note: OBSERVED 2026-08-30T06:16Z: `git add <file> && git commit -F …` was REFUSED with client_slug=1, abs_path=1; immediately after, `framework-purity.js --staged` reported scanned files 0 / 0 violations, and after staging the same file by itself: scanned 1 / 0 violations. The hook fires BEFORE the Bash command executes, so (a) it judged whatever was in the shared index at that instant (another writer — ε commits on this branch — had content staged), and (b) in a combined add+commit command the file being added is NEVER scanned by the hook — the commit that follows the refusal-free path carries unscanned bytes. Two failure modes: false refusal on someone else's staged content; false clearance of one's own. Workaround applied tonight (not a bypass): stage, run --staged by hand, commit as a separate command so the hook judges the real index. No WARPOS_PURITY_GUARD=off used.

AMENDMENT 4 — RESOLUTION IS NOT IDENTITY (beta 5a2d9e17 §3, row 429; instance: E1 d-mtfdwwch-491effca): E1's envelope named the live repo root as 'Your checkout (absolute)'; the path RESOLVED (amendment-2's check would pass) but was NOT the object named — HEAD was 9de50a49 at 05:45Z and moved four more times during the lane; the lane detected it itself and compensated via git show c88aac1d:<path> (luck, not method). Two DIFFERENT kinds of check, and the lint carries BOTH: (i) resolution — the reference reaches something; (ii) identity — the thing reached IS the object the envelope claims (for a checkout: git rev-parse HEAD in that directory equals the pin; for a file: sha equals the stated sha). Standing rule for briefs (beta): the NON-FRAMING verification — 'run git rev-parse HEAD; if it does not equal QUALIFYING_PIN, say so and stop' — goes in EVERY brief including the lane that grades content, because it names no artifact content and cannot frame; E3 had it, E1 did not, and E1 was the lane pointed at a moving tree.
